boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Dartmouth College
boards.description: Late-night dining at Dartmouth is a mix of campus-run staples and local Hanover favorites that keep students fueled through long study sessions and social nights.

cards.title: FoCo Late Night
cards.subtitle: The Central Dining Hub
cards.notes: Reopens from 9:30 PM to 1:30 AM for à la carte fried favorites like chicken tenders and mozzarella sticks. It is the primary social gathering spot after dark.
cards.short_summary: The main dining hall's late-night session offering comfort food and a lively social atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: The Class of 1953 Commons reopens for late-night dining from 9:30 p.m. to 1:30 a.m. daily.
cards.source_title: Dining Locations | Dartmouth Dining
cards.access_notes: Open daily 9:30 PM - 1:30 AM during the academic year.

cards.title: The Library Lifeline
cards.subtitle: Baker-Berry Library
cards.notes: Located in the library, this spot is essential for late-night study sessions, offering coffee, snacks, and pre-packaged meals until 2:00 AM.
cards.short_summary: A high-traffic cafe inside the main library providing caffeine and snacks for late-night studiers.
cards.evidence_claim: Novack Cafe serves as a late-night alternative for students working in the library, often open until 2 a.m.
cards.source_title: They Are What They Eat | Dartmouth Alumni Magazine
cards.access_notes: Typically open until 2:00 AM on weeknights during terms.

cards.title: Late Night Collis
cards.subtitle: Collis Student Center
cards.notes: Known for made-to-order pasta and stir-fry, this student center staple reopens at 9:30 PM for a more customized late-night meal.
cards.short_summary: A student center cafe offering customizable hot meals like pasta and smoothies during late hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Collis Cafe reopens at 9:30 p.m. for Late Night, offering pasta, chicken tenders, and paninis.
cards.source_title: COLLIS CAFE - Life at Dartmouth
cards.access_notes: Late-night hours typically start at 9:30 PM.

cards.title: The 24/7 Engineering Hub
cards.subtitle: Engineering & Computer Science Center
cards.notes: An automated snack bar open 24/7, providing coffee, tea, and a variety of snacks for students in the West End of campus.
cards.short_summary: A fully automated, 24/7 snack bar located in the Thayer School of Engineering building.
cards.evidence_claim: Back of the Napkin is a 24/7 snack bar in the Engineering and Computer Science building.
cards.source_title: Late Night Food Options! - Dartmouth Admissions
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

cards.title: Molly's Weekend Run
cards.subtitle: South Main Street
cards.notes: A local favorite for wood-fired pizzas and truffle fries, staying open until midnight on Fridays and Saturdays for late-night diners.
cards.short_summary: A popular Hanover restaurant known for its bread and honey butter, offering late hours on weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: Molly's Restaurant is open until midnight on Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Molly's Restaurant & Bar
cards.access_notes: Open until 12:00 AM on Friday and Saturday; 10:00 PM other nights.

cards.title: The Lou's Challenge
cards.subtitle: South Main Street
cards.notes: A legendary tradition where students pull an all-nighter and wait for Lou's to open at 6:00 AM for a celebratory breakfast.
cards.short_summary: A historic diner and bakery central to the 'Lou's Challenge' all-nighter tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Students participate in the 'Lou's challenge' by staying up all night to be at Lou's when they open at 6 a.m.
cards.source_title: Places to Eat in Hanover | Dartmouth Admissions
cards.access_notes: Opens at 6:00 AM on weekdays; 7:00 AM on weekends.

cards.title: The On-Campus Bodega
cards.subtitle: Collis Student Center
cards.notes: The go-to spot for late-night snacks, frozen meals, and dorm essentials, conveniently located in the basement of the student center.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus convenience store providing snacks and essentials during evening hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Collis Market is an on-campus convenience store located in the lower level of the Collis Student Center.
cards.source_title: Dining Locations | Dartmouth Dining
cards.access_notes: Hours vary by term; typically open late for student convenience.

cards.title: Ramunto's Pizza Run
cards.subtitle: South Street
cards.notes: A staple for New York-style brick oven pizza, popular for group orders and quick slices before the 9:00 PM closing.
cards.short_summary: A local pizzeria known for its brick oven pies and proximity to campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Ramunto's Brick & Brew is located on South Street and serves brick oven pizza.
cards.source_title: Hanover Brick & Brew - Ramunto's
cards.access_notes: Open until 9:00 PM most nights.

cards.title: BocaSoca Burritos
cards.subtitle: South Main Street
cards.notes: Formerly Boloco, this spot remains a favorite for burritos and bowls, serving the community until 9:00 PM on most days.
cards.short_summary: A Mexican-inspired grill offering burritos and bowls in the heart of Hanover.
cards.evidence_claim: BocaSoca (formerly Boloco) is located at 35 South Main St and is open until 9 p.m. Monday-Saturday.
cards.source_title: BOCASOCA Mexican Grill
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Saturday until 9:00 PM.

cards.title: Sawtooth Late Bites
cards.subtitle: Allen Street
cards.notes: An underground venue offering a full kitchen until 10:00 PM, providing a modern space for late-evening meals and live entertainment.
cards.short_summary: A subterranean restaurant and stage offering evening dining and cultural events.
cards.evidence_claim: Sawtooth Kitchen's kitchen is open nightly until 10:00 p.m.
cards.source_title: Sawtooth Kitchen | Hanover
cards.access_notes: Kitchen open until 10:00 PM nightly.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the specific study nooks, social lounges, and quiet retreats that Dartmouth students use to navigate their daily academic and social lives beyond the standard tour stops.

cards.title: Afternoon Tea at Sanborn
cards.subtitle: Sanborn House
cards.notes: Visit at 4:00 PM on weekdays for the long-standing tradition of free tea and low-cost cookies served in a wood-paneled English department library.
cards.short_summary: A historic library hosting a daily afternoon tea tradition with free tea and cookies for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Sanborn Library offers a tea service each weekday afternoon at 4 o'clock, a tradition dating back to the 1930s.
cards.source_title: A Teatime Tradition Begins in Sanborn Library
cards.access_notes: Open to students; tea service is typically 4:00 PM - 5:00 PM during academic terms.

cards.title: The Tower Room Retreat
cards.subtitle: Baker-Berry Library
cards.notes: Head to the second floor of Baker Library for a silent, high-ceilinged space with comfortable armchairs and large windows overlooking the campus.
cards.short_summary: A quintessential silent study hall located on the second floor of the historic Baker Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Tower Room is a quiet study and contemplation space in the historic Baker Library, often cited by students for its 'Hogwarts' atmosphere.
cards.source_title: Classrooms and Spaces | Dartmouth Libraries
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; strictly silent study environment.

cards.title: One Wheelock Coffee House
cards.subtitle: Collis Student Center
cards.notes: Relax in this lower-level student lounge that offers a coffee-house vibe, free coffee/tea, and frequent evening student performances.
cards.short_summary: A student-run lounge in the Collis Center providing free beverages and a social atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: One Wheelock, located in the lower atrium of Collis, serves as a coffee house style student lounge with free coffee and tea.
cards.source_title: Student Center Facilities | Collis Center
cards.access_notes: Accessible to students via the lower level of Collis; check for evening event schedules.

cards.title: Fairchild Fourth Floor Views
cards.subtitle: Fairchild Center
cards.notes: Find a table on the top floor to study with floor-to-ceiling windows and a view of the Foucault Pendulum in the atrium below.
cards.short_summary: A modern, light-filled study area in the physical sciences complex known for its expansive windows.
cards.evidence_claim: The 4th floor of the Sherman Fairchild Physical Sciences Center is a student-favored study spot due to its natural light and views.
cards.source_title: My Favorite Study Spot | Dartmouth Admissions
cards.access_notes: Open during academic building hours; typically quieter than the main libraries.

cards.title: Rauner Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Webster Hall
cards.notes: Study in the bright, glass-enclosed reading room of Webster Hall, surrounded by the college's rare books and archives.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, sunlit study space housed within the college's special collections library.
cards.evidence_claim: Rauner Special Collections Library in Webster Hall offers a brightly-lit, quiet reading room and mezzanine for student study.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Rauner Special Collections
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 9:00 AM - 5:45 PM; bags must be stored in lockers.

cards.title: Irving Institute Atrium
cards.subtitle: West End
cards.notes: Utilize the modern collaboration spaces and radiant-heated floors in this sustainable building, which also houses the Fern Café.
cards.short_summary: A high-tech, sustainable building on the West End featuring open study areas and a cafe.
cards.evidence_claim: The Irving Institute building offers a range of open work, study, and collaboration spaces and is open to the public during business hours.
cards.source_title: The Irving Institute Building
cards.access_notes: Open to the public 7 AM - 8 PM weekdays; swipe access for the Dartmouth community until 11 PM.

cards.title: The 'Blobby' Social Hub
cards.subtitle: Baker Library Lobby
cards.notes: Join the social hum of 'Blobby' (Baker Lobby), where students meet for group projects or casual conversation near the Cafe@Baker.
cards.short_summary: The main lobby of Baker Library, colloquially known as 'Blobby,' used for social study.
cards.evidence_claim: Officially named Reiss Hall, 'Blobby' is the student-preferred term for Baker Library's lobby, used for group projects and meeting friends.
cards.source_title: Dartmouth Libraries 101
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 for students with ID; public access during library hours.

cards.title: Arts Forum Atrium
cards.subtitle: Visual Arts Center
cards.notes: Study in the three-story central atrium of the BVAC, a space designed for cross-disciplinary interaction near the Nearburg Gallery.
cards.short_summary: A modern three-story atrium in the visual arts building used for study and student exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arts Forum is a three-story central atrium at the heart of the Visual Arts Center designed to promote the sharing of ideas.
cards.source_title: Black Family Visual Arts Center at Dartmouth College
cards.access_notes: Open during academic building hours; ground floor includes a public gallery.

cards.title: Kresge Library Quiet Zone
cards.subtitle: Fairchild Hall
cards.notes: Visit the 3rd floor of Fairchild Hall for a quiet library focused on STEM resources with views of the surrounding campus greenery.
cards.short_summary: A specialized library for physical sciences offering quiet carrels and group study tables.
cards.evidence_claim: Kresge Library, located on the 3rd floor of Fairchild Hall, offers quiet study spaces and collections for the physical sciences.
cards.source_title: About Kresge Library
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; typically less crowded than Baker-Berry.

cards.title: Common Ground Lounge
cards.subtitle: Collis Student Center
cards.notes: Use this main-floor lounge for casual study or socializing; it features comfortable furniture and a fireplace when not hosting events.
cards.short_summary: A versatile student lounge and event space in the heart of the Collis Student Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Common Ground is a popular student lounge space outfitted with comfortable furniture and a fireplace when not used for programs.
cards.source_title: Student Center Facilities | Collis Center
cards.access_notes: Open to students; check the Collis calendar for event-related closures.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover free social activities and public spaces at Dartmouth College, from world-class art galleries and historic murals to scenic river trails and community gardens.

cards.title: Explore Global Art Collections
cards.subtitle: 6 East Wheelock Street
cards.notes: Visit one of the oldest college museums in the US to view over 65,000 works. Admission is always free for students and the public during gallery hours.
cards.short_summary: A teaching museum with diverse global collections and free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission to the Hood Museum is always free, which makes it easier to come back another day.
cards.source_title: Visiting with Children | Hood Museum - Dartmouth
cards.access_notes: Open Wednesday-Friday 11am-5pm and Saturday 10am-5pm; closed Sunday-Tuesday.

cards.title: View the Orozco Murals
cards.subtitle: Baker-Berry Library Basement
cards.notes: Walk through the lower level of Baker Library to see Jose Clemente Orozco's monumental fresco cycle, a National Historic Landmark accessible during library hours.
cards.short_summary: A massive 24-panel fresco cycle depicting the history of the Americas.
cards.evidence_claim: José Clemente Orozco's extraordinary mural cycle The Epic of American Civilization (1932-34) is located in Dartmouth's Baker Library.
cards.source_title: Orozco's Epic - Dartmouth - Hood Museum
cards.access_notes: Accessible during Baker-Berry Library public hours, typically until midnight during terms.

cards.title: Visit the Rooftop Greenhouse
cards.subtitle: Class of 1978 Life Sciences Center
cards.notes: Take the elevator to the 4th floor to explore the Brout Orchid Collection and tropical plant rooms. Public hours are offered three days a week.
cards.short_summary: A rooftop botanical facility featuring diverse plant collections and study space.
cards.evidence_claim: THE GREENHOUSE IS OPEN TO EVERYONE! Public Hours: Tuesday, Wednesday, and Friday 10am - 2:30pm.
cards.source_title: Visit - Dartmouth
cards.access_notes: Open to the public Tuesday, Wednesday, and Friday from 10:00 AM to 2:30 PM.

cards.title: Picnic by the Connecticut River
cards.subtitle: Lyme Road
cards.notes: Head three miles north of campus to enjoy riverside benches, picnic spots, and walking trails. The farm is open for public enjoyment anytime.
cards.short_summary: A 220-acre educational farm with public trails and river access.
cards.evidence_claim: We invite you to come to the O Farm anytime to enjoy our setting! We have benches down by the river which are perfect for picnicking.
cards.source_title: FARM - Dartmouth Sustainability Office
cards.access_notes: Open to the public daily; located approximately 3 miles north of the main campus.

cards.title: Browse Rare Books and Archives
cards.subtitle: Webster Hall
cards.notes: Visit the reading room in historic Webster Hall to view rare manuscripts or the college archives. The library is open to the public for research and curiosity.
cards.short_summary: A public-access library housing rare books and Dartmouth's historical records.
cards.evidence_claim: We are open to the public. Many people enjoy using our brightly-lit, quiet space to study.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Dartmouth Libraries
cards.access_notes: Public reading room and mezzanine study space available during standard library hours.

cards.title: Take a 'Woccom' Around the Pond
cards.subtitle: Hilton Field Lane
cards.notes: Join the local tradition of a 'walk around Occom.' The flat loop path is a popular spot for students to decompress and enjoy the changing seasons.
cards.short_summary: A scenic recreational pond with a popular perimeter walking path.
cards.evidence_claim: Occom is one of the most popular routes frequented by Dartmouth students. It's common for students to go on a 'Woccom'.
cards.source_title: Favorite Hanover Walks | Dartmouth Admissions
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible year-round; the path is flat and suitable for walking or jogging.

cards.title: Relax in a Memorial Garden
cards.subtitle: Maple Street & Downing Road
cards.notes: Find peace in this naturalized acre featuring a gazebo, swing, and over 40 species of wildflowers. It is a privately owned space open for public reflection.
cards.short_summary: A tranquil community garden and wildflower sanctuary near campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Nathan's Garden honors the memory of Nathan Hall... the garden has become a favorite retreat for residents, students, and visitors.
cards.source_title: Nathan's Garden - Hanover Conservancy
cards.access_notes: Open to the public; located less than half a mile from downtown Hanover.

cards.title: Cross the State Border
cards.subtitle: West Wheelock Street
cards.notes: Walk across the Connecticut River to stand on the border of New Hampshire and Vermont. The bridge offers wide pedestrian paths and views of the river valley.
cards.short_summary: A bridge connecting Hanover, NH and Norwich, VT with scenic river views.
cards.evidence_claim: The bridge connects Hanover, New Hampshire, and Norwich, Vermont, so you can stand right on the border if you read the signs.
cards.source_title: Favorite Hanover Walks | Dartmouth Admissions
cards.access_notes: Public bridge with pedestrian sidewalks; accessible 24/7.

cards.title: Attend Free Student Programming
cards.subtitle: 2 North Main Street
cards.notes: Check the schedule for weekly trivia nights, bingo, and coffeehouse concerts. Most events organized by the Programming Board are free for the campus community.
cards.short_summary: The hub for student activities, hosting frequent free social events.
cards.evidence_claim: The Collis Student Center also hosts weekly trivia nights, bingo nights, concerts and other performances that are open to all students.
cards.source_title: What Do Dartmouth Students Do For Fun?
cards.access_notes: Events are typically held in the evenings; check the Collis digital displays for current schedules.

cards.title: Hike Along the Connecticut River
cards.subtitle: South Main Street Trailhead
cards.notes: Follow this 1.1-mile trail from South Main Street for a wooded walk along the riverbank. It is part of the local 'green necklace' of conservation lands.
cards.short_summary: A moderate wooded trail offering scenic views of the Connecticut River.
cards.evidence_claim: River Trail, 1.1 miles: Runs from the electric substation on South Main Street to the corner of Maple Street and Downing Road.
cards.source_title: Trail Descriptions | Hanover, NH
cards.access_notes: Public trail accessible from dawn to dusk; trailhead located near the electric substation on S. Main St.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: From the silent stacks of Baker-Berry to the historic tea service at Sanborn, these ten campus environments offer distinct atmospheres for focused academic work.

cards.title: Baker Library Tower Room
cards.subtitle: Baker-Berry Library, 2nd Floor
cards.notes: Work in a quintessential academic setting with large windows and comfortable armchairs. This silent space is ideal for long reading sessions and focused individual study.
cards.short_summary: A historic, silent reading room in Baker Library known for its traditional atmosphere and campus views.
cards.evidence_claim: The Tower Room is located on the second floor of Baker Library and is described as a quiet space with couches, chairs, and views of the outdoors.
cards.source_title: A Guide to Study Spots | Dartmouth Admissions
cards.access_notes: Open until midnight during the week and 2:00 AM on weekends for students.

cards.title: Sanborn Library
cards.subtitle: Sanborn House
cards.notes: Study in a wood-paneled room that hosts a daily tea tradition at 4:00 PM. It offers a quiet, scholarly environment with leather armchairs and heavy wooden tables.
cards.short_summary: A historic English Department library famous for its daily afternoon tea service and dark academia aesthetic.
cards.evidence_claim: Sanborn Library offers a tea service each weekday afternoon at 4:00 PM and features butternut paneling and leather armchairs.
cards.source_title: A Teatime Tradition Begins in Sanborn Library - Dartmouth
cards.access_notes: Tea is served weekdays 4:00 PM–5:00 PM; the space is a quiet study area outside of tea hours.

cards.title: 1902 Room
cards.subtitle: Baker Library, Level 1
cards.notes: Utilize this 24-hour study space for late-night sessions. It features soft seating and a normal noise level, making it suitable for both group and individual work.
cards.short_summary: A popular 24/7 study room in Baker Library offering a mix of soft seating and table space.
cards.evidence_claim: The 1902 Room is open 24 hours a day and is one of the most popular rooms in the library for individual or group study.
cards.source_title: Spaces | Dartmouth Libraries
cards.access_notes: Accessible 24/7 with a valid Dartmouth ID.

cards.entity_name: Rauner Special Collections Library Reading Room
cards.title: Rauner Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Webster Hall
cards.notes: Work in the brightly-lit Rooke Reading Room surrounded by rare manuscripts. Follow strict reading room protocols, such as using pencils only and storing bags in lockers.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, high-ceilinged reading room in Webster Hall used for studying and accessing special collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Rauner Library's reading room is a brightly-lit, quiet space where visitors are welcome to study following specific expectations.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Rauner Special Collections Library
cards.access_notes: Open to the public during business hours; personal belongings must be stored in provided lockers.

cards.title: Sherman Art Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Carpenter Hall
cards.notes: Find a quiet spot among the art reference collections. The room features soaring windows and crafted wooden paneling, providing a serene environment for visual research.
cards.short_summary: A specialized library space for art and architecture students featuring natural light and quiet study carrels.
cards.evidence_claim: Sherman Art Library has two study rooms with the Art Reference Collection and quiet study spaces on lower levels.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Sherman Art Library
cards.access_notes: Located in Carpenter Hall; accessible from North Main Street or through Baker-Berry Library.

cards.title: Irving Institute Atrium
cards.subtitle: Irving Institute for Energy & Society
cards.notes: Collaborate in this modern, energy-efficient building. The atrium offers comfortable seating and a cafe, making it a preferred spot for group meetings and informal study.
cards.short_summary: A contemporary, high-ceilinged atrium in the West End designed for collaboration and informal interaction.
cards.evidence_claim: The Irving building offers a range of open work, study, and collaboration spaces, including an atrium open to the public.
cards.source_title: The Irving Institute Building | Dartmouth
cards.access_notes: Open to the public weekdays 7:00 AM–8:00 PM; swipe access for the Dartmouth community until 11:00 PM.

cards.entity_name: Black Family Visual Arts Center Arts Forum
cards.title: BVAC Arts Forum
cards.subtitle: Black Family Visual Arts Center
cards.notes: Study on the ground floor red couches within this three-story atrium. The space is surrounded by studios and galleries, offering a creative and modern atmosphere.
cards.short_summary: A central three-story atrium in the visual arts building used for study and cross-disciplinary interaction.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arts Forum is a three-story central atrium at the heart of the Visual Arts Center, with ground floor seating used for study.
cards.source_title: My Five Favorite Study Spots at Dartmouth (Updated!)
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible during building hours; features large picture windows facing the Arts Plaza.

cards.title: Feldberg Study Tables
cards.subtitle: Murdough Center
cards.notes: Access large tables and individual carrels in the West End's primary library. It is a quiet hub for business and engineering students with access to Bloomberg Terminals.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative library space serving the Tuck and Thayer schools with dedicated research tools.
cards.evidence_claim: Feldberg Library has large tables, individual study spaces, and reservable study rooms within the Murdough Center.
cards.source_title: Feldberg Business & Engineering Library
cards.access_notes: General public hours are typically 8:00 AM–8:00 PM; subject librarians available weekdays.

cards.title: Kresge Library
cards.subtitle: Fairchild Hall, 3rd Floor
cards.notes: Enjoy quiet study with views of the campus from the third floor. This library supports the physical sciences and offers rolling whiteboards and public computers.
cards.short_summary: A quiet library in the Fairchild Physical Sciences Center known for its views and specialized collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Kresge Library is located on the 3rd floor of Fairchild Hall and offers quiet study spaces and great views.
cards.source_title: About Kresge Library - Dartmouth
cards.access_notes: Open during academic terms; check library website for current seasonal hours.

cards.title: Collis Common Ground
cards.subtitle: Collis Student Center
cards.notes: Study in the heart of campus life. This versatile lounge space is often used for informal gatherings and individual work between classes.
cards.short_summary: The iconic central lounge and event space within the Collis Student Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Common Ground is an iconic student lounge and event space in the Collis Student Center, open for informal use.
cards.source_title: About the Collis Student Center - Dartmouth
cards.access_notes: Open daily until 1:00 AM; accessible to all students.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the essential streets and corridors surrounding Dartmouth College, from the historic storefronts of Main Street to the emerging residential hubs of West Wheelock.

cards.title: The Town's Front Door
cards.subtitle: South Main Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk this primary commercial strip to find student staples like Lou's Restaurant and the Dartmouth Co-op, located just steps from the Green.
cards.short_summary: The central commercial corridor of downtown Hanover featuring historic local businesses and student-focused retail.
cards.evidence_claim: South Main Street is described as the heart of Hanover's downtown hub, featuring long-standing businesses like the Dartmouth Co-op and Lou's Restaurant.
cards.source_title: A walk down Main Street: Reflecting on recent changes - The Dartmouth
cards.access_notes: Public sidewalk access; business hours vary by establishment.

cards.title: The Bookstore Block
cards.subtitle: Allen Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit this side street to find Still North Books & Bar, a popular multi-use space where students study among bookshelves and coffee.
cards.short_summary: A short commercial side street known for its cozy bookstore-cafe and local dining options.
cards.evidence_claim: Still North Books & Bar is located on Allen Street and serves as a significant off-campus study spot for Dartmouth students.
cards.source_title: A Guide to Study Spots | Dartmouth Admissions
cards.access_notes: Public street access; Still North is a primary destination here.

cards.title: Global Dining Row
cards.subtitle: Lebanon Street Corridor
cards.notes: Head here for a variety of international cuisines, including student favorites like Han Fusion and Jewel of India.
cards.short_summary: A major east-west street south of the Green hosting several popular international restaurants.
cards.evidence_claim: Lebanon Street is home to several student-frequented restaurants including Tacos y Tequila, Han Fusion, and Jewel of India.
cards.source_title: Places to Eat in Hanover | Dartmouth Admissions
cards.access_notes: Public street access; restaurants typically open for lunch and dinner.

cards.title: The Residential Gateway
cards.subtitle: West Wheelock Corridor
cards.notes: Observe the new high-density student housing developments that serve as a major gateway between the campus and the Ledyard Bridge.
cards.short_summary: A primary thoroughfare undergoing significant redevelopment to include new Dartmouth residence halls.
cards.evidence_claim: Dartmouth and the Town of Hanover are collaborating on streetscape improvements for West Wheelock Street to complement new residence halls.
cards.source_title: Dartmouth, Hanover Collaborate on W. Wheelock Upgrades
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare; construction active through 2026.

cards.title: The Bakery Block
cards.subtitle: South Street Corridor
cards.notes: Find Umpleby's Bakery & Cafe here, a quiet spot favored by students for breakfast sandwiches and daytime study sessions.
cards.short_summary: A quieter street south of the main downtown hub featuring mixed-use housing and local cafes.
cards.evidence_claim: Umpleby's Bakery & Cafe is located at 3 South Street and is noted as a popular spot for student dates and study.
cards.source_title: Best First Date Spot in Hanover - The Dartmouth
cards.access_notes: Public street access; Umpleby's typically closes by 3 PM.

cards.title: The House Community Corridor
cards.subtitle: East Wheelock Corridor
cards.notes: Walk past the East Wheelock House residential cluster and the historic Wheelock House, the original home of the college founder.
cards.short_summary: A street bordering the Green that connects the central campus to residential house communities.
cards.evidence_claim: East Wheelock Street hosts the East Wheelock House residential community and the historic Wheelock House.
cards.source_title: East Wheelock House | Office of Residential Life
cards.access_notes: Public street; residential buildings require student ID for entry.

cards.title: The Real Estate Hub
cards.subtitle: Currier Place Corridor
cards.notes: Locate the Dartmouth Real Estate Office here, which manages many of the off-campus commercial and residential properties in town.
cards.short_summary: A small street housing administrative offices and nearby apartment complexes for the Dartmouth community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dartmouth Real Estate Office is located at 4 Currier Place and manages commercial listings in downtown Hanover.
cards.source_title: Commercial Space | Dartmouth Real Estate Office
cards.access_notes: Public street; office hours are typically standard business hours.

cards.title: The Co-op Grocery Block
cards.subtitle: South Park Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit the Hanover Co-op Food Store, a community-owned grocery staple for students living in nearby off-campus apartments.
cards.short_summary: A residential and commercial street known for its community grocery store and graduate student housing.
cards.evidence_claim: South Park Street is home to the Hanover Co-op and is a common location for student apartment subleases.
cards.source_title: Hanover – dartlist - Sites at Dartmouth
cards.access_notes: Public street; Co-op grocery store open daily.

cards.title: The Administrative Edge
cards.subtitle: North Main Street Corridor
cards.notes: Pass by Robinson Hall and other administrative buildings that line the western edge of the Dartmouth Green.
cards.short_summary: The northern extension of Main Street where the town's commercial district meets the college's administrative core.
cards.evidence_claim: Robinson Hall is located at 6 North Main Street and houses various student organization offices.
cards.source_title: East Wheelock House | Office of Residential Life
cards.access_notes: Public street and sidewalk bordering the Green.

cards.title: The Market Corridor
cards.subtitle: College Street Corridor
cards.notes: Look for seasonal community events like the farmers market that occasionally take place along this street bordering the eastern campus.
cards.short_summary: A street running along the eastern edge of the campus, hosting residential life and community events.
cards.evidence_claim: College Street is noted for hosting seasonal farmers markets and being part of the tight-knit Dartmouth neighborhood.
cards.source_title: Living in the Heart of Hanover - Upper Valley Real Estate
cards.access_notes: Public street; event schedules vary seasonally.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Explore the unique rituals and historic celebrations that define the Dartmouth experience, from icy pond plunges to century-old mountain excursions.

cards.title: Circling the Homecoming Bonfire
cards.subtitle: Dartmouth Night & Homecoming
cards.notes: Join the first-year class in running laps around a massive multi-story bonfire on the Green, a tradition dating back to 1888 to celebrate community and class spirit.
cards.short_summary: A massive bonfire built by first-years and circled by the class during Homecoming weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: The first bonfire was lit 136 years ago in 1888; first-years traditionally run around it a set number of times based on their class year.
cards.source_title: The Homecoming Bonfire: A history of administrative changes - The Dartmouth
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually on Friday night of Homecoming weekend on the Dartmouth Green.

cards.title: The Occom Pond Polar Bear Swim
cards.subtitle: Winter Carnival
cards.notes: Brave the icy waters of Occom Pond during Winter Carnival by plunging into a hole cut through the ice, a rite of passage for students since the early 20th century.
cards.short_summary: A Winter Carnival tradition where students jump into a hole cut in the ice of Occom Pond.
cards.evidence_claim: Participants are secured by a rope and leap into a carved-out section of the icy water at Occom Pond during the annual Winter Carnival.
cards.source_title: Watching the Polar Bear Swim - Dartmouth Admissions
cards.access_notes: Held during Winter Carnival weekend at Occom Pond; safety ropes and EMS are present.

cards.title: First-Year Trips (DOC Trips)
cards.subtitle: Pre-Orientation Tradition
cards.notes: Embark on a student-led outdoor adventure before classes begin, ranging from hiking to organic farming, concluding with a celebratory stay at Moosilauke Ravine Lodge.
cards.short_summary: A massive student-run pre-orientation program involving outdoor excursions and community building.
cards.evidence_claim: Over 90 percent of the freshman class participates in these outdoor excursions, which conclude at the Moosilauke Ravine Lodge.
cards.source_title: First-Year Trips | Dartmouth Outdoors
cards.access_notes: Required registration for incoming students; trips depart from Robinson Hall.

cards.title: The Baker Tower Bell Chimes
cards.subtitle: Daily Campus Soundscape
cards.notes: Listen for the daily 6:00 PM ringing of the Alma Mater from the Baker-Berry Library tower, a tradition maintained by student bell ringers since 1928.
cards.short_summary: Daily musical performances played on the 16-bell carillon in the Baker Library tower.
cards.evidence_claim: The bells play the Alma Mater daily at 6:00 PM and vary pieces during class breaks; they are operated by a student bell ringer.
cards.source_title: Baker Tower Bells | Department of Music - Dartmouth
cards.access_notes: Heard across campus; the tower itself has limited public access for tours.

cards.title: Ledyard's Trip to the Sea
cards.subtitle: Ledyard Canoe Club
cards.notes: Follow the path of John Ledyard by paddling 218 miles down the Connecticut River to the Long Island Sound, a grueling multi-day rite for senior club members.
cards.short_summary: An annual 218-mile canoe trip from Hanover to the ocean, honoring explorer John Ledyard.
cards.evidence_claim: Each May, students in the Ledyard Canoe Club re-trace John Ledyard's 1773 river trek from Hanover to Old Saybrook.
cards.source_title: History of the Ledyard Canoe Club - Hanover Inn Dartmouth
cards.access_notes: Departs from the Ledyard Canoe Club boathouse on the Connecticut River in May.

cards.title: The Annual Dartmouth Powwow
cards.subtitle: Mother's Day Weekend
cards.notes: Experience one of the largest student-run events in the Northeast, celebrating Indigenous cultures with traditional dancing, drumming, and crafts on the Green.
cards.short_summary: A major cultural celebration of Native American and Indigenous traditions held annually on the Green.
cards.evidence_claim: The Powwow has been held since 1972 and attracts upwards of 1,500 people to the Green every Mother's Day weekend.
cards.source_title: Powwow - Native American Program - Dartmouth
cards.access_notes: Open to the public; held on the Dartmouth Green (Leede Arena in case of rain).

cards.title: The Twilight Ceremony
cards.subtitle: Orientation Finale
cards.notes: Gather at the Bema on the eve of fall classes to receive a candle flame passed from the graduating class, symbolizing the start of your Dartmouth journey.
cards.short_summary: A candle-lighting ceremony at the Bema marking the official entrance of first-years into the community.
cards.evidence_claim: Members of the most recent graduating class pass the flame to the newest incoming class at the Bema before fall classes begin.
cards.source_title: Twilight Ceremony | The William Jewett Tucker Center - Dartmouth
cards.access_notes: Held at the Bema (outdoor amphitheater) on the Sunday evening before fall term.

cards.title: Carrying the Senior Canes
cards.subtitle: Commencement Tradition
cards.notes: Spot graduating seniors carrying hand-carved wooden walking sticks topped with symbols like the Sphinx or Griffin, denoting membership in various senior societies.
cards.short_summary: A graduation tradition where seniors carry carved canes representing their secret or senior societies.
cards.evidence_claim: Graduates carry canes carved with symbols like a Griffin or Sphinx as the only public display of senior society membership.
cards.source_title: Canes Show Connection at Commencement - Dartmouth
cards.access_notes: Visible during the Commencement procession on the Green in June.

cards.title: Green Key Weekend Concerts
cards.subtitle: Spring Big Weekend
cards.notes: Celebrate the arrival of spring with a massive outdoor concert on the Gold Coast lawn and block parties along Webster Avenue during this premier social weekend.
cards.short_summary: A major spring festival featuring a mainstage concert and campus-wide celebrations.
cards.evidence_claim: Green Key refers to the annual mainstage concert and campus-wide celebration held every spring term.
cards.source_title: 2026 Green Key festivities - Madison Wuu - Dartmouth Admissions
cards.access_notes: Concert is free for students with a wristband; guest tickets are available for purchase.

cards.title: Winter Carnival Ice Sculptures
cards.subtitle: Winter Carnival
cards.notes: View elaborate ice carvings on the Green created by student teams, a tradition that has transformed the campus into a winter gallery since 1910.
cards.short_summary: A competitive and artistic display of ice and snow sculptures on the Dartmouth Green.
cards.evidence_claim: The Winter Carnival features an iconic ice sculpture showcase as part of its century-old festivities.
cards.source_title: A Carnival to Remember | Dartmouth Admissions
cards.access_notes: Sculptures are displayed publicly on the Green throughout Winter Carnival weekend.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Dartmouth College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Kick Off Your Arrival
cards.subtitle: Orientation Check-In at Mass Row
cards.notes: Start your journey by picking up your Dartmouth ID and room keys at the check-in tents. House Community leaders will be there to welcome you to your new home.
cards.short_summary: The official starting point for new students to receive IDs and housing keys.
cards.evidence_claim: Orientation Check-In, ID and Key Pick-Up, and House Community Welcome for students occurs at Massachusetts Row during assigned times.
cards.source_title: Arrival and Move-in - New Student Orientation - Dartmouth
cards.access_notes: Check-in typically runs from 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. on scheduled arrival days.

cards.title: Bond with Your 'Trippees'
cards.subtitle: Outdoor Orientation Tradition
cards.notes: Join a student-led group for hiking, organic farming, or nature writing. It is a cornerstone tradition for meeting classmates before fall term classes begin.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing student-run outdoor orientation program for incoming freshmen.
cards.evidence_claim: First-Year Trips are a student-run orientation program run by the Dartmouth Outing Club since 1935, offering activities like climbing and organic farming.
cards.source_title: First-Year Trips - Dartmouth Admissions
cards.access_notes: Participation is optional but highly encouraged for all incoming first-year students.

cards.title: Refuel at 'FoCo'
cards.subtitle: The Main Campus Dining Hall
cards.notes: Grab a meal at the various stations, from the omelet bar to Ma Thayer's. It is the social hub for first-year students on the Ivy Unlimited meal plan.
cards.short_summary: The primary all-you-care-to-eat dining facility on the Dartmouth campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Class of 1953 Commons, known as FoCo, features multiple food stations including a vegan station and Ma Thayer's for daily selections.
cards.source_title: What I Eat in a Day at Dartmouth!
cards.access_notes: Open daily for breakfast, lunch, and dinner; requires a meal plan swipe or payment.

cards.title: Explore the Stacks
cards.subtitle: Academic Heart of Campus
cards.notes: Visit the Orozco murals and find your favorite study nook. The library is a central hub for research, advising, and late-night academic sessions.
cards.short_summary: The main library complex at Dartmouth, home to significant murals and study spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Baker-Berry Library is a hub for learning at the center of campus, offering academic resources and the famous Orozco murals.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Dartmouth Libraries
cards.access_notes: Open daily; Berry Library typically stays open until 12:00 a.m. for students.

cards.title: Get Inspired by Art
cards.subtitle: Free Campus Art Museum
cards.notes: Walk through the galleries to see global collections. Admission is always free, making it an easy spot to visit with new friends between orientation sessions.
cards.short_summary: A teaching museum with a diverse collection of art from around the world.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission to the Hood Museum of Art is always free for everyone, and it offers student-led tours and events.
cards.source_title: College Students | Hood Museum - Dartmouth
cards.access_notes: Open Wednesday-Friday 11am-5pm and Saturday 10am-5pm.

cards.title: Late Night Fun
cards.subtitle: Weekend Student Activities
cards.notes: Head to the Collis Center for late-night food, concerts, and comedy. These events provide a safe, alcohol-free social environment every Friday and Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A student-led program providing late-night entertainment and social events.
cards.evidence_claim: Collis After Dark offers late-night social and entertainment events every Friday and Saturday, including concerts and food.
cards.source_title: Collis After Dark | Collis Center for Student Involvement
cards.access_notes: Events typically take place late on Friday and Saturday nights.

cards.title: Walk the River Trails
cards.subtitle: Nature Escape Near Campus
cards.notes: Take a break from the bustle of orientation with a walk along the Connecticut River. The trails are easily accessible from the north end of campus.
cards.short_summary: A 100-acre forested park with trails adjacent to the Dartmouth campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Pine Park features over 100 acres of forested land and trails parallel to the Connecticut River, popular for student walks.
cards.source_title: Favorite Hanover Trails | Dartmouth Admissions
cards.access_notes: Open daily from dawn to dusk for foot travel.

cards.title: Touch History
cards.subtitle: Rare Books and Archives
cards.notes: Visit Webster Hall to see rare manuscripts and the college archives. It's a quiet, brightly-lit space where you can get hands-on with primary sources.
cards.short_summary: The home of Dartmouth's rare books, manuscripts, and college archives.
cards.evidence_claim: Rauner Special Collections Library houses over 100,000 rare books and the Dartmouth College Archives in Webster Hall.
cards.source_title: Rauner Special Collections Library
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 9:00 a.m. to 5:45 p.m.

cards.title: Sunday Morning Tradition
cards.subtitle: Classic Hanover Diner
cards.notes: Enjoy a hearty breakfast or a famous baked good at this Main Street staple. It's a favorite spot for students to gather and recap their first weekend.
cards.short_summary: An iconic Hanover diner and bakery serving the Dartmouth community since 1947.
cards.evidence_claim: Lou's Restaurant & Bakery is a cornerstone of the Dartmouth experience, known for its breakfast and the 'Lou's Challenge' tradition.
cards.source_title: Cafés in Hanover: Part 7 (Lou's Bakery) - Dartmouth Admissions
cards.access_notes: Opens early at 6:30 a.m. daily; popular for breakfast and brunch.

cards.title: Find Your Community
cards.subtitle: Club and Organization Fair
cards.notes: Browse hundreds of student organizations on the Green. This is the best time to sign up for clubs, from a cappella groups to the outing club.
cards.short_summary: An annual fair where students can learn about and join campus organizations.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Involvement Fair is held before classes begin, allowing students to learn about hundreds of clubs and organizations.
cards.source_title: Orientation | Collis Center for Student Involvement
cards.access_notes: Typically held on the Green the day before fall term classes begin.
